cases.name: tuple-write-order
cases.description: #132 TUPLE-WRITE-ORDER: for `(lhs0, lhs1, ...) = rhs`, solc resolves ALL LHS lvalue references up front left-to-right (a later component's index/key observes PRE-STORE state), then performs the stores RIGHT-TO-LEFT (when two components alias the same location the LEFTMOST assignment wins). Repros: `(x,x)=(1,2)` (local, x==1), `(arr[0],arr[0])=(1,2)` (storage, arr[0]==1), and `arr[0]=5; (arr[0], arr[arr[0]])=(1,2)` where the second index sees arr[0]==5 so it writes arr[5]=2 then arr[0]=1 giving (arr[0],arr[1],arr[5])==(1,0,2). solidity-lean formerly recursed head-first and interleaved resolve-then-write, giving the rightmost aliased write and observing earlier writes; the fix resolves all LHS refs left-to-right then stores right-to-left. Forge deploys on pinned solc/EVM and asserts the values; Lean imports the same source and runs the source semantics.

cases.name: typemin-bounds
cases.description: TYPEMIN: `type(intN).min` for N < 256 must lower to the two's-complement negative word `2^256 - 2^(N-1)`, not the raw positive `2^(N-1)`. solc pushes 0xff..ff80 for int8.min (=-128), 0xff..ff80..00 for int128.min (=-2^127), 0x80..00 for int256.min (=-2^255); `type(int8).min == -128` is true and `type(int8).min + 1 == -127`. Forge and imported Lean pin the interpreter's signed-min lowering, comparison, arithmetic, and return ABI-encoding.

evals.label: importedTypeMinBoundsSemantics
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.TypeMinBounds.importedSourceUnit
  let target := "TypeMinBounds"
  let empty := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let word := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let sint := fun (v : Int) => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord v)
  let callVals := fun (name : String) (expected : List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value) =>
    SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedCallValuesMatch 64 source target name empty [] expected
  let r1 <- callVals "int8Min" [sint (-128)]
  let r2 <- callVals "int128Min" [sint (-(2^127 : Int))]
  let r3 <- callVals "int256Min" [sint (-(2^255 : Int))]
  let r4 <- callVals "int8MinNarrow" [sint (-128)]
  let r5 <- callVals "int128MinNarrow" [sint (-(2^127 : Int))]
  let r6 <- callVals "int8MinEqNeg128" [word 1]
  let r7 <- callVals "int8MinPlusOne" [sint (-127)]
  Except.ok (r1 && r2 && r3 && r4 && r5 && r6 && r7))

cases.name: compound-cleanup
cases.description: Compound assignment (+= *= <<= ...) to a narrow (<256-bit) int/uint LValue applies the LValue-type-width cleanup solc emits: checked Panic 0x11 for arithmetic overflow, truncating cast for <<=, unchecked wrap; covers local/mapping/array/struct LValues and the already-correct uint256 control.

cases.name: callpos-remainder
cases.description: CALLPOS-REMAINDER closes the two highest-reachability remaining call-position over-rejects. Bug 1: a compound-assign RHS containing a user call (`total += fee()`, `m[k] += f()`, `x += this.g()`) routed through the env-aware pure lowering, which returns none for any call RHS, so solidity-lean over-rejected the whole function; the fix hoists the call into a prefix statement and feeds the pure temp-read result as the RHS of the SAME assignOpCleanupExpr node, preserving the LValue-width COMPOUND-CLEANUP (Panic 0x11 on narrow `+=`, truncating `<<=`); solc evaluates the RHS call FIRST (verified via --ir: `x += f()`/`m[k] += f()` emit the call before the LValue read/index). Bug 2: a direct storage array `.push(<call>)` whose argument is a user call (`xs.push(f())`, `xs.push(this.g())`) had no lowering for the call arg; the fix hoists the call, then pushes the temp-read through the existing storageArrayPushRef path (restricted to receivers with no dynamic index, matching solc's evaluate-arg-then-push order). Internal variants pin acceptance AND runtime (including two eval-order pins and the narrow-width Panic 0x11 / `<<=` truncation cleanup-preservation controls) via own-call execution; external `this.`-self-call variants pin acceptance via importedContractAccepted and are executed by the Forge test.

cases.name: overreject-callpos-batch
cases.description: OVERREJECT-CALLPOS-BATCH closes three confirmed call-position over-rejects (solc 0.8.35 legacy accepts + compiles each; the model used to reject the whole contract at Source->Executable). A: `T x = outer(inner())` — a direct internal call whose argument is itself a direct internal call; the single-binding varDecl arm never hoisted the nested-call argument, so it is now hoisted into a prefix temp before the outer call (solc order inner-before-outer, verified via --ir). B: `T x = m[f()]` / `y = m[f()]` / `T z = m[f()] + 1` — an internal call used as a mapping/array index in a non-return read position; the index-call hoist existed only in the return arm, so an `Expr.index base (call)` arm was added to the single-return expression hoister (reusing `indexReadCoreBuilder?`) and the generic varDecl / plain-assign fallbacks were routed through it (base is a pure reference, so hoisting the index call preserves solc order). E: `m[f()] = g()` — an index-assign whose index and RHS are both calls; on pure-RHS failure the RHS call is hoisted into the RHS temp before the index call, preserving solc RHS-before-index order (verified via --ir: g() before f()). Everything is own-call executable (internal calls + mappings), so acceptance AND runtime are pinned by own-contract execution, including two eval-order pins (orderCompose = 12 requires inner-before-outer; writeIdxOrder = 21 requires RHS-before-index). Call-free controls pin the pre-existing pure paths; the Forge test re-checks every case against real solc/EVM.

cases.name: mapping-index-internal-call
cases.description: MI1: an INTERNAL function-call result used AS a mapping/array INDEX, in both the lvalue (`m[idu8(k)] = v`) and rvalue (`return m[idu8(k)]`) positions, for a uint256-valued mapping, a narrow (uint8) valued mapping, and a dynamic array. solc accepts these (ordinary Solidity); solidity-lean formerly over-rejected at Executable lowering because the index operand of an index-access had no internal-call hoisting fallback. The fix hoists the index call into a temp (as constructor bodies / state-var initializers already do) and threads the temp through the index; the RHS is bound before the hoisted index call so evaluation order matches solc (RHS before LHS index, pinned by runOrder == 21). Forge deploys on pinned solc/EVM and asserts the values; Lean imports the same source and runs the source semantics.

cases.name: free-fn-nested-arg
cases.description: FREE-ARG: a FREE (file-level) function call nested in the ARGUMENT position of another call — outer(inner(x)) with free outer/inner (return position), member(inner(x)) with a free inner nested inside a contract member (return position), struct-passing sum(mk(1,2)) with free mk/sum, and sink(inner(x)) as a bare expression statement. solc accepts and runs these; solidity-lean formerly over-rejected the WHOLE contract at Executable lowering because FunctionDecl.directOrPtrCallArgReturnTy? (the return-type gate guarding the nested-argument hoist) took only the contract-member functions list and dropped freeFunctions, so a nested free callee's return type resolved to none. The fix threads freeFunctions into that gate (mirroring internalCalleeReturnTys? / abiTyWithInternalFunctionsEnv?). Forge deploys on pinned solc/EVM and asserts the values; Lean imports the same source and runs the source semantics. Two nested-arg positions remain scoped OUT as separate pre-existing gaps that affect MEMBER calls identically (orthogonal to this fix): a varDecl initializer (uint y = outer(inner(x)) — the arm needs a storage-ref return) and a double-nested call (outer(inner(inner(x))) — the single-level hoist does not recurse).

cases.name: tuple-lhs-index-call
cases.description: TUP-IDX: a tuple ASSIGNMENT whose LHS component is indexed by an INTERNAL function call — `(xs[f()], z) = (3, 4)` (array), `(m[k()], z) = (8, 9)` (mapping), two call-valued indices with call-valued RHS (`(xs[tick(1)], ys[tick1(2)]) = (rhs(3), rhs(4))`), and a call in BOTH an LHS index and the RHS (`(xs[keyf()], z) = (rhs(3), 9)`). solc accepts and runs these (the index call runs once); solidity-lean formerly over-rejected at Executable lowering because the tuple-LHS lvalue lowering had no internal-call hoisting for the index operand (the out-of-scope sibling of MI1). The fix hoists each call-valued LHS index into a per-component temp and builds the tuple target from it. Evaluation order matches solc — RHS components left-to-right, THEN LHS index expressions left-to-right — pinned by runOrder's logv == 3412. Forge deploys on pinned solc/EVM and asserts the values + order; Lean imports the same source and runs the source semantics.

cases.name: contract-ordered-compare
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM ordered comparisons (`<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`) on two contract-typed operands (and `this`), comparing their addresses as unsigned 160-bit values (solc emits only deprecation warning 9170); the forge test asserts each operator equals the unsigned comparison of the two deployed addresses plus irreflexivity/reflexivity/antisymmetry and this<this/this<=this; pinned solc rejects ordered comparison of DIFFERENT unrelated contract types (no common type). Lean imports the whole source unit from solc AST: `importedContractAccepted` covers that the common typechecker now ACCEPTS ordered comparison of same-type contract operands AND interface operands (InterfaceOrderedCompare.ltIface) AND base/derived operands upcast to their common base (BaseDerivedOrderedCompare.ltBaseDerived) — previously an over-reject: relational routed through the context-free `commonImplicit?` which omitted contracts entirely and could not resolve a base/derived pair; the fix accepts two contract operands in the lt/gt/le/ge dispatch via context-aware bidirectional implicit convertibility (mirroring equality). Runtime witnesses on the own-type target confirm the interpreter compares the contract operands' address words unsigned, matching solc's bools on seeded deterministic addresses.

cases.name: loop-control
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM while/for loop control; pinned solc and the common checker reject break/continue outside loops; Lean imports the same source contract from solc AST and checks source break/continue behavior.

cases.name: call-position
cases.description: CALL-POSITION over-rejects: a user function call nested in a for/do-while/while CONDITION had no expression lowering and was never wired to the internal-call hoisting machinery, so solidity-lean over-rejected loops solc accepts. The fix desugars a call-bearing condition into the same while(1){ if(cond) ...; body; post } shape used for bare while(f()), re-evaluating the hoisted call each iteration; gated so call-free conditions keep today's loop node, and (for/do-while) only when the body has no bare continue. Internal-call conditions pin acceptance and runtime semantics via own-call execution; a bare external call in a while condition pins acceptance.

cases.name: extcall-binary
cases.description: CLUSTER-B #7 (extcall-binary) over-rejects: an EXTERNAL/member single-return call nested inside a BINARY operand (`require(t.balanceOf(a) >= amt)`, `uint y = t.n() + 1`, `x = t.n() + 1`, `while (i < t.limit())`, `if (t.ok() && cond)`, `if (cond || t.ok())`, `return t.n() + g`) had no expression lowering — the recursive binary/condition hoister recognised only INTERNAL ident calls, so solidity-lean over-rejected whole functions solc accepts. The fix widens the same seam: when exactly one operand is a single external member call and the other is pure, the call is lowered via the existing tryExternalCall machinery in its source position (solc legacy left-to-right), bound to a temp, and the operand replaced by the temp; `&&`/`||` with the call on the right materialise the short-circuit as an ifElse on the pure-lhs temp. Uses external `this.`-self-calls (STATICCALLs), so importedContractAccepted pins acceptance (lowering) and the Forge test exercises real solc/EVM execution.

cases.name: shortcircuit-callpos
cases.description: SHORTCIRCUIT-CALL-POS (#131) over-rejects — the residual of the EXT-CALL-POS family (#70/#73/extcall-binary). Three call-in-short-circuit / call-in-ternary positions solc 0.8.35 accepts but solidity-lean failed to LOWER: (1) BOTH operands external calls in `&&`/`||` (`this.f() && this.g()`); (2) an EXTERNAL-call ternary CONDITION (`this.f() ? a : b`); (3) a call nested in an otherwise-pure operand (`h() && (j()+1>0)`). The runtime short-circuit was already correct — purely a lowering coverage gap. The fix mirrors the both-internal `&&`/`||` hoister for both-external, hoists an external-call ternary condition like the internal one, and hoists a pure-operand's inner call INSIDE the guarded branch so it runs exactly when the lhs selects it. Uses `this.`-self-calls (STATICCALL/CALL) so importedContractAccepted pins acceptance (lowering); the Forge test exercises real solc/EVM execution and PROVES short-circuit via a `_counter` witness (0 when the effectful operand is skipped, 1 when it runs).

cases.name: shortcircuit-pure-operand
cases.description: SHORTCIRCUIT-CALL-POS (#131) case 3 — a call nested in an otherwise-pure operand of `&&`/`||` (`h() && (j()+1>0)`), with PURELY INTERNAL calls so the contract is EXECUTABLE in the solidity-lean model. The semantics eval RUNS the contract in-model and proves short-circuit is preserved: `skipPanic` (`hFalse() && (1/jZero()>0)`) and `skipPanicOr` (`hTrue() || (1/jZero()>0)`) return normally because the div-by-zero in the SKIPPED operand does not execute, while `runPanic` (`hTrue() && (1/jZero()>0)`) reverts Panic 0x12 because the SELECTED operand is genuinely lowered and evaluated. The Forge lane pins the same behaviour (plus a `_counter` effect witness) on real solc/EVM.

evals.label: importedShortCircuitSemantics
evals.expr:
(
  let src := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ShortCircuitPureOperand.importedSourceUnit
  let callN := fun (fn : String) =>
    SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract 64 src
      "ShortCircuitPureOperandTarget"
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name fn)
      SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  let retWord := fun (fn : String) (v : Nat) =>
    match callN fn with
    | Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _
        [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word w]) =>
        SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq w v
    | _ => false
  let panics := fun (fn : String) =>
    match callN fn with
    | Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _
        (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.panic code)) => code == 0x12
    | _ => false
  retWord "skipPanic" 0 &&
  retWord "skipPanicOr" 1 &&
  panics "runPanic" &&
  retWord "pureOperand" 1)

cases.name: qualified-callee
cases.description: QUAL-CALLEE (#74/#77): emit/revert/require whose callee is a MEMBER access (Base.BaseHit, Base.BaseErr, self QualifiedCalleeHarnessTarget.LocalHit/LocalErr) rather than a bare identifier. solc 0.8.35 accepts these; solidity-lean previously over-rejected them (emit at the executable lowering; base-/self-qualified revert and require at the type checker AND lowering). Lean imports the same source unit from solc AST and checks the qualified-callee emit event topics/data and the base-/self-qualified custom-error revert name+args, including the require(cond, Base.Err(a)) form. Library-/interface-qualified errors (L.Bad) remain declined (see docs/DECISIONS.md).

evals.label: importedQualifiedCalleeSemantics
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.QualifiedCallee.importedSourceUnit
  let word := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let empty := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let target := "QualifiedCalleeHarnessTarget"
  let callName := fun (fn : String) (args : List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value) =>
    SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract 64 source target (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name fn) empty args
  let eventOk := fun (result : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult) (name : String) (signature : String) (v : Nat) =>
    match result with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state [] =>
        match state.events with
        | [event] => event.name == name && event.topics == [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Keccak.digestWord signature] && event.dataBytes == SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordToBytesBE SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordBytes v
        | _ => false
    | _ => false
  let revertOk := fun (result : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult) (name : String) (v : Nat) =>
    match result with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.custom errName [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word w]) =>
        errName == name && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq w v
    | _ => false
  let baseEmit <- callName "emitBaseHit" [word 4]
  let selfEmit <- callName "emitSelfHit" [word 9]
  let baseRevert <- callName "revertBaseErr" [word 5]
  let selfRevert <- callName "revertSelfErr" [word 6]
  let reqRevert <- callName "requireBaseErr" [word 0]
  Except.ok
    (eventOk baseEmit "BaseHit" "BaseHit(uint256)" 4 &&
     eventOk selfEmit "LocalHit" "LocalHit(uint256)" 9 &&
     revertOk baseRevert "BaseErr" 5 &&
     revertOk selfRevert "LocalErr" 6 &&
     revertOk reqRevert "BaseErr" 0))

evals.label: importedTrySuccess
evals.expr:
(do
  let output ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalWordOutput 5
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalResult
    SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall
    "ok(uint256)"
    [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256]
    [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 4]
    output
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.TryCatch.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "TryCatchHarnessCaller"
  let callResult ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [result] []) contract "read"
    { contract.core.context with accountCodes := [(0xbeef, [1])] }
    SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
    [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 0xbeef, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 4]
  match callResult with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word value] =>
      let observation := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.resultState callResult
      match observation.externalInteractions with
      | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
          Except.ok
            (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq value 5 &&
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall 0xbeef result.calldata 0 none &&
              call.success && call.output == output)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  | _ => Except.ok false)

        { contract.core.context with accountCodes := [(0xbeef, [1])] }

        [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 0xbeef]

  | none => Except.ok false)

cases.name: custom-error
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM custom-error revert bytes; pinned solc and the common checker reject reserved custom-error names, duplicate error parameter names, custom-error overloading, unknown custom-error reverts, data-location annotations, and local-error shadowing of a free error with the wrong argument shape; Lean imports the same source contract from solc AST and checks abstract custom-error name and arguments.

evals.label: importedCheckCustomError
evals.expr:
(do
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.ownCall 32 SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.CustomError.importedContract (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "check") SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 20]
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.custom name [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word value, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word limit]) =>
      Except.ok (name == "TooBig" && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq value 20 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq limit 10)
  | _ => Except.ok false)

(do

  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.custom name [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.bytes reason, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.bytes payload]) =>
      Except.ok (name == "DynamicBad" && reason == [99, 97, 116] && payload == [1, 2, 3])
  | _ => Except.ok false)

evals.expr:

cases.name: receive-fallback-dispatch
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM receive/fallback dispatch, typed fallback raw calldata return, function-selector precedence over fallback, missing receive/fallback rejection, and inherited/overridden fallback dispatch; Lean imports the same source contracts from solc AST and checks the abstract source ABI dispatch semantics.

evals.label: importedReceiveFallbackAndSelectorDispatch
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ReceiveFallbackDispatch.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackDispatch"
  let word := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let empty := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let encodeWord := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeWord
  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let receiveResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract empty 0xc0de 0xbeef 0 []
  let receiveSnapshot <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract receiveResult.state 0xc0de 0xbeef 0 (selector "snapshot()")
  let expectedReceive <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.address, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word 2, word 0xbeef, word 0, word 0]
  let fallbackPayload := [0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef, 1, 2]
  let fallbackResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract receiveResult.state 0xc0de 0xbeef 0 fallbackPayload
  let fallbackSnapshot <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract fallbackResult.state 0xc0de 0xbeef 0 (selector "snapshot()")
  let expectedFallback <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.address, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word 1, word 0xbeef, word 0, word fallbackPayload.length]
  let touchResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract fallbackResult.state 0xc0de 0xabcd 0 (selector "touch(uint256)" ++ encodeWord 9)
  let touchSnapshot <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldataAtFrom 128 contract touchResult.state 0xc0de 0xabcd 0 (selector "snapshot()")
  let expectedTouchSnapshot <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.address, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word 9, word 0xabcd, word 0, word fallbackPayload.length]
  Except.ok (receiveResult.success && receiveResult.output == [] && receiveSnapshot.success && receiveSnapshot.output == expectedReceive && fallbackResult.success && fallbackResult.output == [] && fallbackSnapshot.success && fallbackSnapshot.output == expectedFallback && touchResult.success && touchResult.output == encodeWord 10 && touchSnapshot.success && touchSnapshot.output == expectedTouchSnapshot))

evals.label: importedTypedFallbackMissingAndOverrideDispatch
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ReceiveFallbackDispatch.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let empty := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let payload := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
  let bytesContract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackBytes"
  let bytesResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 bytesContract empty payload
  let onlyFallback <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackOnlyFallback"
  let onlyFallbackEmpty <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 onlyFallback empty []
  let onlyReceive <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackOnlyReceive"
  let onlyReceiveEmpty <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 onlyReceive empty []
  let onlyReceiveUnknown <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 onlyReceive empty [0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]
  let missing <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackMissing"
  let missingUnknown <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 missing empty [0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]
  let missingEmpty <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 missing empty []
  let child <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackChild"
  let childReceive <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 child empty []
  let childFallback <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 child childReceive.state [0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]
  let overrideContract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReceiveFallbackOverride"
  let overrideReceive <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 overrideContract empty []
  let overrideFallback <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 64 overrideContract overrideReceive.state [0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]
  Except.ok (bytesResult.success && bytesResult.output == payload && onlyFallbackEmpty.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (onlyFallbackEmpty.state.loadSlot 0) 3 && onlyReceiveEmpty.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (onlyReceiveEmpty.state.loadSlot 0) 4 && !onlyReceiveUnknown.success && onlyReceiveUnknown.output == [] && !missingUnknown.success && missingUnknown.output == [] && !missingEmpty.success && missingEmpty.output == [] && childReceive.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (childReceive.state.loadSlot 0) 5 && childFallback.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (childFallback.state.loadSlot 0) 6 && overrideReceive.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (overrideReceive.state.loadSlot 0) 7 && overrideFallback.success && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (overrideFallback.state.loadSlot 0) 8))

cases.name: contract-creation
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM child deployment from a factory; Lean imports both same-file contracts from solc AST and checks the abstract source contract-creation request/result.

evals.label: importedContractCreationRequest
evals.expr:
(do
  let constructorArgs ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 4]
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ContractCreation.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ContractCreationHarnessFactory"
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 32 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [] [ { contractName := "CreatedChild", constructorArgs := constructorArgs, success := true, address := 0xc0de } ]) contract "make"
    (contract.core.context)
    SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
    [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 4]
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word address] =>
      let observation := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.resultState result
      match observation.externalInteractions with
      | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.contractCreation create] =>
          Except.ok
            (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq address 0xc0de &&
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ContractCreationResult.matches create "CreatedChild" constructorArgs 0 none &&
              create.success &&
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq create.address 0xc0de)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  | _ => Except.ok false)

evals.label: importedBaseConstructorRuntimeArgSemantics
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.BaseConstructorRuntimeArgs.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let state := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty

  let construct := fun fuel responder name context sender value args =>
    SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.constructContractWithContextUnderResponder fuel responder program name context state sender value args
  let seedOk := fun result expected =>
    match result with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state [] =>
        match state.storage.toList with
        | [(0, value)] => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq value expected
        | _ => false
    | _ => false
  let blockBase <- ctxFor "BlockArg"
  let blockCtx := { blockBase with blockEnv := { SolidCore.Solidity.Source.BlockEnv.empty with number := 50 } }
  let block <- construct 512 [] "BlockArg" blockCtx 0 0 []
  let senderCtx <- ctxFor "SenderArg"
  let sender <- construct 512 [] "SenderArg" senderCtx 0x1234 0 []
  let valueCtx <- ctxFor "ValueArg"
  let paid <- construct 512 [] "ValueArg" valueCtx 0 9 []
  let nonpayableCtx <- ctxFor "NonpayableValueArg"
  let nonpayable <- construct 512 [] "NonpayableValueArg" nonpayableCtx 0 0 []
  let freeBase <- ctxFor "FreeCallArg"
  let freeCtx := { freeBase with blockEnv := { SolidCore.Solidity.Source.BlockEnv.empty with number := 50 } }
  let free <- construct 512 [] "FreeCallArg" freeCtx 0 0 []
  let freeUsing <- construct 512 [] "FreeUsingArg" (<- ctxFor "FreeUsingArg") 0 0 []
  let libraryUsing <- construct 512 [] "LibraryUsingArg" (<- ctxFor "LibraryUsingArg") 0 0 []
  let contractUsing <- construct 512 [] "ContractUsingArg" (<- ctxFor "ContractUsingArg") 0 0 []
  let modifierParam <- construct 512 [] "ModifierParamArg" (<- ctxFor "ModifierParamArg") 0 0 [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 8]
  let balanceBase <- ctxFor "BalanceArg"
  let balanceCtx := { balanceBase with self := 0xcafe, accountBalances := [] }
  let balance <- construct 512 [] "BalanceArg" balanceCtx 0 10 []
  let externalCalldata <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalCalldata "seed()" [] []
  let externalOutput <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalWordOutput 41
  let externalOracle : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
    { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall, target := 0xbeef, calldata := externalCalldata, value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := externalOutput }
  let externalBase <- ctxFor "ExternalCallArg"
  let externalCtx := { externalBase with accountCodes := [(0xbeef, [1])] }
  let external <- construct 512 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [externalOracle] []) "ExternalCallArg" externalCtx 0 0 []
  let externalOk :=
    match external with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state [] =>
        seedOk external 41 &&
          match state.externalInteractions with
          | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall 0xbeef externalCalldata 0 none && call.success && call.output == externalOutput
          | _ => false
    | _ => false
  let thisCalldata <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalCalldata "seedSource()" [] []
  let thisOutput <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedHighLevelExternalWordOutput 13
  let thisOracle : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
    { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall, target := 0xcafe, calldata := thisCalldata, value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := thisOutput }
  let thisBase <- ctxFor "ThisCallArg"
  let thisCtx := { thisBase with self := 0xcafe }
  let thisCall <- construct 512 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [thisOracle] []) "ThisCallArg" thisCtx 0 0 []
  let thisOk :=
    match thisCall with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state [] =>
        seedOk thisCall 13 &&
          match state.externalInteractions with
          | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall 0xcafe thisCalldata 0 none && call.success && call.output == thisOutput

    | _ => false

cases.name: tuple-literal-hoist

cases.name: internal-fn-pointers
cases.description: Stage-C pin for the boundary-completion arc (docs/refs-completion-solc-research.md §2): internal function pointers as dispatch IDs — 8-byte storable state variable round-trip, pointer as internal argument and return, data-dependent (ternary) pointers, uninitialized-pointer call -> Panic(0x51), and recursion through a runtime pointer.

cases.name: fnptr-internal-eq
cases.description: Pin for internal function-pointer equality/inequality (#50, FP-EQ): `fp == g` / `fp != h` compare dispatch identity and return a bool; solc 0.8.35 legacy (optimizer=false) compiles them, whereas solidity-lean previously reverted with Panic(0)/typeMismatch (BinaryOp.apply eq/ne arms lacked a Value.internalFunction case). Covers direct-name eq/ne, two pointers to the same function, and reassignment. Ternary-initialized and storage-read pointer comparison is a separate lowering gap (docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-07-09) and is not asserted here.

cases.name: fnptr-internal-eq-derived
cases.description: Pin for internal function-pointer equality/inequality on pointers PRODUCED through a ternary initializer or a STORAGE-field read (#53, FP-EQ-2; follow-up to #50 FP-EQ / the fnptr-internal-eq lane which covers only direct-name assignment). solc 0.8.35 legacy (optimizer=false) compiles `fp == g` / `fp != g` to a dispatch-identity compare regardless of how `fp` was produced; solidity-lean previously lowered a ternary/storage-derived pointer to a plain Value.word and reverted/mis-typed on comparison (internalFunction == word -> typeMismatch). The FP-EQ-2 fix carries Value.internalFunction through every typed lowering context. Covers ternary-init eq/ne (both branches) and storage round-trip eq/ne.

cases.name: storage-uninit-fn-ptr
cases.description: G17 pin (docs/solidity-lean-solc-deep-comparison.md): an internal function pointer held in a never-assigned STORAGE state variable (and one left unset on an untaken constructor branch) has the zero dispatch value; calling it panics 0x51. Storage-default counterpart of the already-laned local-uninitialized pointer call; ground truth from pinned-solc/EVM Forge (both revert with Panic(0x51)).

Pinned solc accepts both (warnings only) and virtual dispatch reaches the override bodies; ground truth from Forge (runTag(5)=7, runBump(5)=25). Lean imports the same source and own-calls the derived entrypoints, pinning acceptance + value.

Ground truth from Forge: viaUint(21)=42, viaInt(-4)=-12, viaBytes(0xaabbcc,10)=13, viaBool(false)=true. Lean imports the same source and own-calls each entrypoint, pinning dispatch across uint/int/bytes/bool receivers.

cases.name: array-mutation-usingfor
cases.description: #135 ARRAY-MUTATION-VS-USINGFOR: builtin push/pop exist ONLY on STORAGE dynamic arrays (and storage bytes). On a MEMORY/calldata array the builtin does not exist, so `m.pop()`/`m.push(v)` must dispatch through using-for to the attached library function (solc lowers `m.pop()` to `MemArrLib.pop(m)`). solidity-lean formerly intercepted the name push/pop for ANY array receiver and demanded a storage lvalue, over-rejecting these (Div1). Forge ground truth: viaMemoryPop()=3, viaMemoryPush()=7, viaCalldataPop([_,_,_,_])=4. Lean imports the same source and own-calls each entrypoint, pinning memory/calldata using-for dispatch. Div2 (over-accept): a storage arr.push(7) that ALSO has an attached L.push is AMBIGUOUS -> solc rejects "Member push not unique after argument-dependent lookup"; pinned by solc_rejects and the model witness arrayMutationUsingForDisciplineMatches.

cases.name: utf8-string-literal
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter compare solc's UTF-8 lowering of a regular (non-`unicode`) string literal containing a non-ASCII code point (U+00E9 via a backslash-u escape): bytes length, the two UTF-8 bytes 0xC3 0xA9, keccak256 of bytes(...), and abi.encodePacked all use the UTF-8 encoding rather than the raw code point.

cases.name: unicode-nonbmp
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter agree that a unicode"..." literal containing a NON-BMP code point (U+1F600 GRINNING FACE) lowers to its 4 UTF-8 bytes 0xF0 0x9F 0x98 0x80 - not a UTF-16 surrogate pair. Pins bytes length, individual UTF-8 bytes, and keccak256(bytes(...)) for a pure emoji and a mixed ASCII+BMP(U+4F60)+non-BMP string, plus solc's rejection of bytes2(unicode"...") (4 bytes > 2). Regression guard for the importer, which previously ascii-escaped the code point to a surrogate pair that Lean decoded to null bytes.

cases.name: nonutf8-string-literal
cases.description: Forge, pinned solc, and the imported Lean interpreter agree that a plain (non-`unicode`, non-`hex"..."`) string literal whose bytes are NOT valid UTF-8 (`"\xff\x00\x41"` == 0xFF 0x00 0x41) has type `literal_string hex"ff0041"`: it converts to `bytes` (accepted, in both `bytes(...)` and `bytes memory =` contexts) but NOT to `string` (rejected). solc omits the AST `value` field for such a literal and keeps only `hexValue`; the importer previously died on the missing `value` and now falls back to `hexValue`, lowering the literal exactly like a `hex"..."` literal (Lean type Ty.bytes). Pins bytes length, individual raw bytes 0xFF/0x00/0x41, keccak256(bytes(...)), and solc's rejection of the string-context conversion.

cases.name: abi-memory-eager
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter compare solc's eager per-element validation of a memory-location aggregate ABI parameter versus lazy per-access validation of a calldata aggregate: a dirty (out-of-range uint8) element that is never read reverts empty for a memory uint8[]/struct parameter but succeeds for the calldata counterpart that only reads .length / a clean sibling.

evals.label: memoryEagerVsCalldataLazyMatrix
evals.expr:
(do
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.AbiMemoryEager.importedSourceUnit
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "AbiMemoryEager"
  let encodeWord := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeWord
  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let dirtyArray := encodeWord 32 ++ encodeWord 1 ++ encodeWord 256
  let dirtyPair := encodeWord 7 ++ encodeWord 256
  let call := fun signature args => SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 256 contract SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty (selector signature ++ args)
  let memArray <- call "memArrayLength(uint8[])" dirtyArray
  let cdArray <- call "cdArrayLength(uint8[])" dirtyArray
  let memPair <- call "memPairFirst((uint8,uint8))" dirtyPair
  let cdPair <- call "cdPairFirst((uint8,uint8))" dirtyPair
  Except.ok (!memArray.success && memArray.output == [] && cdArray.success && cdArray.output == encodeWord 1 && !memPair.success && memPair.output == [] && cdPair.success && cdPair.output == encodeWord 7))

cases.name: packed-ternary-width
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter compare solc's abi.encodePacked width for a conditional operand: abi.encodePacked(cond ? a : b) with a uint8 then-branch and a uint16 else-branch packs the result using the ternary's common type (uint16 -> 2 bytes) in both branches, pinned via keccak256 of the packed bytes.

cases.name: ternary-bytesn-common-type
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter compare a conditional `c ? x : y` whose branches are `bytesN` of different widths (bytes4 then, bytes2 else). solc inserts the implicit conversion of each branch to the common type bytes4; because bytesN is left-aligned, widening bytes2 0xaabb to bytes4 keeps content in the HIGH bytes -> 0xaabb0000 for the return value, abi.encode, and abi.encodePacked. An integer-ternary control (uint8/uint256) locks in that narrow-int branches are unaffected.

cases.name: completeness-boundaries
cases.description: Completeness boundaries C1-C4 (2026-07-08). Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this repo's typechecker both REJECT: (C1) `string.length` (must use `bytes(s).length`), (C2) `type(ConcreteContract).interfaceId` (only interface/abstract are non-deployable and expose interfaceId), (C3) `abi.encodePacked` of an array whose element is dynamically sized (`bytes[]`,`string[]`). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors: `bytes(s).length` and `uint[].length`; `type(Interface).interfaceId` and `type(Abstract).interfaceId`; `abi.encodePacked(uint[])`. C4: constant `%` with a negative operand is VALID and folds to the truncated remainder (sign of dividend): (-7)%3==-1, 7%(-3)==1, (-7)%(-3)==-1 (was over-rejected). solc source: Types.cpp ArrayType::nativeMembers (string has no length), Types.cpp:4271-4285 (type(C) member set gated on deployability), packed-mode nested-dynamic rejection, and constant-expression `%` folding.

cases.name: hash-precompile-builtins
cases.description: Forge pins the sha256 (precompile 0x02) and ripemd160 (precompile 0x03) builtins against real solc 0.8.35 / Foundry-EVM for empty, short, one-word, and >32-byte payloads, plus ripemd160's left-aligned bytes20 result; Lean imports the same solc AST and, under a responder scripted with the SAME EVM ground-truth digests, checks the interpreter forms the precompile STATICCALL calldata (raw payload) and decodes the digest word identically.

evals.label: sha256DigestsMatchEvm
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.HashPrecompiles.importedSourceUnit
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "HashPrecompilesHarnessTarget"
  let ctx := contract.core.context
  let word32 : List Nat :=
    [0x61,0x62,0x63,0x64,0x65,0x66,0x67,0x68,0x69,0x6a,0x6b,0x6c,0x6d,0x6e,0x6f,0x70,
     0x71,0x72,0x73,0x74,0x75,0x76,0x77,0x78,0x79,0x7a,0x30,0x31,0x32,0x33,0x34,0x35]
  let long40 : List Nat := word32 ++ [0x36,0x37,0x38,0x39,0x30,0x31,0x32,0x33]
  let mk := fun (kind : SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind) (data : List Nat) (digest : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) =>
    ({ kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall
       target := SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.address kind
       calldata := data
       value := 0
       gas? := none
       success := true
       output := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordToBytesBE SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordBytes digest }
      : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult)
  let run := fun (fn : String) (kind : SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind) (data : List Nat) (expected : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) => do
    let result := mk kind data expected
    let r ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [result] []) contract fn ctx
      SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.bytes data]
    match r with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word w] =>
        Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq w expected)
    | _ => Except.ok false
  let sha := SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind.sha256
  let s0 ← run "sha256Of" sha [] 0xe3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
  let s1 ← run "sha256Of" sha [1,2,3] 0x039058c6f2c0cb492c533b0a4d14ef77cc0f78abccced5287d84a1a2011cfb81
  let s2 ← run "sha256Of" sha word32 0x653bb1245e828fcda4fa53fcd5a3def5bd7654e651f54b4132b73d74e64435c4
  let s3 ← run "sha256Of" sha long40 0x2fa2c189076e20488be2d1da4af97695cff36f38a0b528347b600f3e3912b353
  Except.ok (s0 && s1 && s2 && s3))

cases.name: block-env-builtins
cases.description: Forge pins BLOCKHASH (blockhash(uint)) and BLOBHASH (blobhash(uint), EIP-4844) against Foundry-EVM with block.number fixed at 1000 via vm.roll: current/future/older-than-256 blocks return 0, the number-1 and number-256 boundary blocks return the deterministic Foundry hashes, and blobhash returns 0 for a non-blob tx. Lean imports the same solc AST and drives the interpreter under a context whose blockHashes map carries the SAME ground-truth hashes plus non-zero decoys at the out-of-window slots, so the interpreter's availability-window predicate (not a map miss) is what forces 0.

evals.label: blockhashBlobhashMatchEvm
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.BlockEnvBuiltins.importedSourceUnit
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "BlockEnvBuiltinsHarnessTarget"
  let base := contract.core.context
  let ctx := { base with
    blockEnv := { base.blockEnv with
      number := 1000
      blockHashes :=
        [ (999, 0xf0222e4555f079f2fdbf570707db75ee508caa46321baeff622a993218303d10)
        , (744, 0x7468eddb0720a03646876d25045fa535478c57a57b912a197efd90e8d667279c)
        , (1000, 0xdead1000)
        , (1001, 0xdead1001)
        , (743,  0xdead0743) ] } }
  let run := fun (fn : String) (arg : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) (expected : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) => do
    let r ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContext 64
      contract fn ctx SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty

    match r with

        Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq w expected)
    | _ => Except.ok false
  let bhCurrent  ← run "blockHashOf" 1000 0
  let bhRecent   ← run "blockHashOf" 999  0xf0222e4555f079f2fdbf570707db75ee508caa46321baeff622a993218303d10
  let bhBoundary ← run "blockHashOf" 744  0x7468eddb0720a03646876d25045fa535478c57a57b912a197efd90e8d667279c
  let bhTooOld   ← run "blockHashOf" 743  0
  let bhFuture   ← run "blockHashOf" 1001 0

(do

cases.name: acceptance-boundaries
cases.description: Acceptance boundaries G2-G10 (2026-07-08). Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this typechecker both REJECT: (G2) msg.value in a non-payable public/external function (TypeError 5887; internal/library/payable exempt), (G3) ==/!= on a reference type bytes/string/array/mapping/struct/UDVT (TypeError 2271), (G4) a compile-time out-of-bounds constant index on a bytesN or fixed-size array (TypeError 1859/3383), (G5) a bare return; with a non-empty (even named) return list (TypeError 6777), (G6) super.f() resolving to an abstract/unimplemented base function (TypeError 9582), (G7) a qualified emit X.g() whose member callee is not an event (TypeError 9292), (G9) an inline array literal of a mapping element type (invalid memory type), and (G10) msg.data inside a receive function (TypeError 7139). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors: msg.value in a payable/internal function; == on address/uint; an in-bounds or dynamic index; a value-carrying/implicit return; super.f() to an implemented base; simple and member-form emits of a real event; an inline array of a value type; and msg.data in an ordinary/fallback function. G8: revert E(...) where a contract-level non-error member (function or state var) shadows a free error E (TypeError 1885); neighbors — a genuine contract error and an unshadowed free error — still revert.

cases.name: array-literal-widen
cases.description: Inline array literal element-widening boundary (task #56 AL1, 2026-07-09). solc 0.8.35 types an inline array literal bottom-up (smallest common mobile element type, e.g. [1,2,3] : uint8[3]) and a fixed->fixed memory-array conversion requires an IDENTICAL element type (ArrayType::isImplicitlyConvertibleTo non-copy branch; no implicit element widening). Pinned solc and this typechecker both REJECT assigning/returning/passing/struct-constructing a literal into a WIDER fixed-array target: uint256[3]=[1,2,3], uint16[3]=[1,2,3], uint256[2][2]=[[1,2],[3,4]], return uint256[3], internal g(uint256[3])([1,2,3]), external this.g([1,2,3]), S(uint256[3])([1,2,3]), and bytes1[2]=[0x11,0x22]; and both still REJECT empty/ragged/fixed->dynamic/element-overflow. Both still ACCEPT (Forge pins runtime values of) the element-matched neighbors: uint8[3]=[1,2,3] (10203), uint256[3]=[uint256(1),2,3] (40606), int8[2]=[int8(-1),2] (255002, order-sensitive), uint8[2][2]=[[1,2],[3,4]] (1234), plus typed bytes1[2] and internal g(uint8[3])([1,2,3]).

cases.name: inline-array-literal-exec
cases.description: AL-EXEC (task #58, 2026-07-09): executable lowering of an inline array literal USED in a function body. solc 0.8.35 types an inline array literal bottom-up (smallest common mobile element type, e.g. [1,2,3] : uint8[3]) and requires the fixed-size memory-array target's element type to EQUAL that bottom-up type. Post-typecheck (AL1) the interpreter previously OVER-REJECTED at executable lowering whenever the elements were undecorated narrow-int literals (uint8[3]=[1,2,3], uint8[2][2]=[[1,2],[3,4]]): the env-less abiTy? of a bare number literal is uint256, so the generic fixed->fixed array conversion saw a uint256[.] source vs the narrow target and failed, aborting the whole contract with `unsupported "checked executable checked contract"`. The fix lowers an inline array literal against a fixed-array target element-wise at the (AL1-verified) target element type. This lane runs each solc-accepted shape through the INTERPRETER via ownCall and pins the SAME runtime value Forge pins on the EVM: var-init narrow (10203), nested/multidim narrow (1234), index-of-literal ([10,20,30][1]=20), inline literal as internal-call argument (sum3([5,6,7])=18), direct return of a fixed memory-array literal ([1,2,3]), and an order-sensitive int8 negative-leading literal (255002).

cases.name: acceptance-boundaries-round2
cases.description: Round-2 acceptance boundaries (2026-07-08) from docs/solc-implementation-divergences-2.md. Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this typechecker both REJECT: (E1) a NON-rational immutable read (keccak256- or constant-ref-initialized) inside a pure function (TypeError 2527; only a RationalNumber initializer stays pure), (O1) a duplicate contract in an override(A,A) list (error 4520), and (PT1) a constant whose value cyclically depends on itself (error 6161). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors on the Lean side: the same immutable read in a view function and a numeric-literal / constant-arithmetic immutable read in pure; the legitimate diamond override(A,B); a non-cyclic constant chain. E2 (over-reject fix): this.f.selector in a pure function is now ACCEPTED while this.f() stays a pure-violation. AE1 confirmed already-handled: abi.encodePacked(bytes[]/string[]) is rejected while encodePacked(uint[]) is accepted.

Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and checks the source ternary mobile-type behavior (G15).

cases.name: ternary-storage-pointer

Forge proves on real EVM that writing through p mutates exactly `b ? s0 : s1` (selected slot written, other untouched), that the member-lvalue form `(b ? s0 : s1).x = v` and a ternary passed to a `storage`-ref param alias the selection too. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST, confirms acceptance (formerly over-rejected), and re-checks the aliasing via own-calls.

Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and checks source nested-tuple assignment behavior (G13).

cases.name: narrow-udvt-arithmetic
cases.description: A narrow (N<256) UDVT `unwrap` yields the underlying `uintN`/`intN`, so checked arithmetic on unwrap results overflows at the narrow width (Panic 0x11) like a plain `uintN`/`intN` — including via a `using`-bound `+` operator; `unchecked{}` still wraps and a 256-bit UDVT is unaffected. Forge pins solc/EVM; Lean checks the paired source-interpreter witnesses (H2 soundness fix).

evals.expr:
(do
  let src := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.NarrowUdvtArithmetic.importedSourceUnit
  let st := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let w := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let i := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int
  let callWord : Nat → String → List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value → Nat → Except SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.TypeError Bool :=
    fun fuel fn args expected => do
      let r ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract fuel src "NarrowUdvtArithmeticHarnessTarget" (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name fn) st args
      match r with
      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word v] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v expected)
      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int v] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v expected)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  let callPanic : Nat → String → List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value → Nat → Except SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.TypeError Bool :=
    fun fuel fn args code => do
      let r ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract fuel src "NarrowUdvtArithmeticHarnessTarget" (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name fn) st args
      match r with
      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.panic c) => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq c code)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  let a1 ← callWord 32 "addU8" [w 100, w 55] 155
  let a2 ← callPanic 32 "addU8" [w 200, w 100] 0x11
  let a3 ← callPanic 32 "addI8" [i 100, i 100] 0x11
  let a4 ← callPanic 32 "subI8" [i (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-100)), i 100] 0x11
  let a5 ← callWord 32 "addI8" [i (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-100)), i 50] (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-50))
  let a6 ← callWord 32 "addU8Unchecked" [w 200, w 100] 44
  let a7 ← callPanic 32 "addU8Operator" [w 200, w 100] 0x11
  let a8 ← callWord 32 "addBig" [w 5, w 6] 11
  Except.ok (a1 && a2 && a3 && a4 && a5 && a6 && a7 && a8))

cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM nested tuple assignment whose RHS contains INTERNAL function calls: a multi-return call filling a nested target `((a,b),c)=(foo(),bar())` (foo returns a 2-tuple), scalar calls in nested RHS positions `((a,b),c)=((g(),h()),k())`, and a hole whose component call still runs. The RHS is evaluated once left-to-right (side effects in that order) then destructured. solc accepts these; solidity-lean formerly over-rejected (nested elaboration could not hoist internal calls). cases.name: storage-array-copy-signed-fixed
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM storage-array copy for the shapes G14 deferred: SIGNED element widening (int8[] -> int16[], sign-extend each element, never overflows) and FIXED-length destinations (T[N] = S[M], N >= M) including signed, with the M..N tail padded 0. solc accepts these (ArrayType::isImplicitlyConvertibleTo); solidity-lean formerly over-rejected (canImplicitlyConvert had no array arm, and the fixed-dest write could not pad). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and runs the source semantics (R2).

cases.name: narrow-arith-widened
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM narrow-integer arithmetic assigned/returned at a WIDER type: solc computes the op at the operands' common type, so a narrow overflow Panics 0x11 even though the result is widened. uint8+uint8 / uint8*uint8 / int8+int8 returned as uint16/int16 panic on operand-width overflow; a non-overflowing add widens; an explicitly-256-bit-widened add (uint256(a)+uint256(b)) does NOT panic. solidity-lean formerly cleaned only at the wider target width and silently produced the fitting wide value (the G15-noted narrow-arithmetic-widened gap). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST.

cases.name: neg-narrow-widened
cases.description: NEG-NARROW (unary analogue of the G15 narrow-arithmetic-widened gap): solc emits negate_t_intN, which negates at the OPERAND width and, in a checked context, guards `if eq(value, intN.min) { panic_error_0x11() }` BEFORE any implicit widening or explicit cast to a wider int. So `-x` of type(intN).min Panics 0x11 in a checked block and wraps to intN.min in an unchecked block, even when returned/assigned/cast as a wider int. solidity-lean formerly ran the checked int256 negation (which never overflows for a narrow intN.min) and cleaned only at the wider target width, silently producing -intN.min in both modes. Forge (real EVM, pinned solc) is the value ground truth: checked -x / int16(-x) of int8.min (and -x of int128.min) Panic 0x11; the unchecked variants wrap to intN.min; a non-min control widens correctly. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST.

cases.name: cf2-revert-pruning
cases.description: CF2 (2026-07-08, docs/DECISIONS.md): solc's ControlFlowRevertPruner prunes the edge after a call to an always-reverting callee, so the storage-pointer-return definite-assignment check (error 3464) runs on the pruned CFG. solidity-lean now computes an always-reverts fixpoint and treats a call to such a callee as terminating, ACCEPTING pick(bool) returns (uint256[] storage p) whose only obligation-unmet path runs through the always-reverting helper alwaysReverts(); importedContractAccepted confirms the fix on the Lean typechecker. Forge (real EVM, pinned-solc compiled) is the value ground truth: the non-reverting path returns xs = [11,22,33] via pickLength/pickAt. (The Lean source Core interpreter does not lower an internal function that returns a storage pointer, a pre-existing limitation orthogonal to CF2, so the value is checked by Forge only.) Pinned solc 0.8.35 REJECTS the sound neighbors — a genuinely-unassigned path, a sometimes-reverting helper, a require(false) helper (require is not an always-revert terminator), and an external this.boom() callee — and the Lean witnesses confirm solidity-lean rejects them too.

cases.description: Round-3 PK1/CL1 boundaries: solc ACCEPTS abi.encodePacked of a nested STATIC array (uint8[2][2], uint8[2][]) with a 32-byte-padded in-place layout, while rejecting a dynamic-element array (uint8[][3]); and solc REJECTS a bare modifier-style base-constructor call (error 1563). Forge/pinned-solc pin the packed layout and the two source rejections; Lean witnesses pin the accept/reject typecheck boundary and the packed byte layout.

Pinned solc rejects an operator binding on a struct target, a `global` directive on a built-in type, a mixed-parameter operator function (UF2), and a duplicate operator binding for one operator+type (UF3); the common checker matches via usingForGlobalNonUdvtDisciplineMatches.

Legacy runs all inline initializers first, so observed reads 0 (the base body has not run yet) while trace ends at 7. cases.name: constructor-target-supplies-indirect-base
cases.description: CTOR-RESIDUE reconciliation (gap #66): the deployment TARGET supplies an INDIRECT base's constructor arguments via a constructor modifier, while the direct inheritor supplies nothing. Target is Mid is Base; Mid (the immediate derived of Base) lists none of Base's arguments, and the most-derived Target supplies them via a constructor modifier Base(3, 4), naming its indirect base. solc permits the constructor-modifier form on any derived contract and evaluates it in that contract's frame, so a == 3, b == 4, and Mid's own constructor runs (m == 7). Minimal reduction of the OpenZeppelin harness pattern (contract Harness is ERC721Enumerable { constructor() ERC721("n","s") {} }). The first CTOR-RESIDUE fix read a base's modifier-supplied arguments only from the base's DIRECT inheritor (Mid), found none, and matched Base's two constructor parameters against zero arguments (arityMismatch "base constructor Base" 2 0). The reconciliation walks the whole linearization to find the actual supplier (the most-derived Target).

      let mOk ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedCallWordMatches 64 SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ConstructorTargetSuppliesIndirectBase.importedSourceUnit "Target" "m" state [] 7

cases.name: overload-shadow
cases.description: OV1 free-function shadowing (2026-07-09). solc removes a file-level (free) function from a contract's name scope whenever a member function (the contract's own — any visibility — or a non-private inherited one) declares the same NAME (name-based shadowing, warning 2519); a single same-named member removes ALL free overloads of that name. Mirrors the shadowing this frontend already implements for errors/events (ErrorSigs/EventSigs.withoutNamesOf) via the new FunctionSigs.withoutNamesOf applied when building env.functions. Over-ACCEPT direction (solc REJECTS): free f(uint256) + member f(string), bare call f(5) has no viable in-scope candidate — now REJECTED (invalid/OV1FreeShadowedByMember.sol; ov1FreeShadowedByMemberRejected). Neighbors stay ACCEPTED: the same shadowing with call f("hi") runs the member, and an unshadowed free f(5) stays callable (ov1ShadowNeighborsAccepted). Over-REJECT direction (solc ACCEPTS): free f(uint256) + same-signature member f(uint256), bare call f(5) runs the MEMBER body (s + 9 == 14, not the free a + 1 == 6); pinned by the real contract's Forge run (testMemberShadowsFree), the frontend now accepting the whole source unit (importedContractAccepted), and the interpreter running g() to 14 (checkedOwnCallWordMatches).

cases.name: modifier-return-reject
cases.description: #54 (MOD-RET, 2026-07-09) from docs/solc-modifier-execution-review.md: solc 0.8.35 REJECTS a `return` that carries ANY expression inside a MODIFIER body — even a void-typed one like `return delete x;` or `return require(true);` — with TypeError 7552 'Return arguments not allowed' (TypeChecker::endVisit(Return), TypeChecker.cpp:1133-1146: a modifier's functionReturnParameters is nullptr). solidity-lean was over-accepting these (its checkReturnExprs keyed only on the empty returnTys and special-cased delete/require/void as allowed, never consulting env.inModifier). Fixed by rejecting any expression-bearing return when env.inModifier. solc_rejects pins solc's compile-time rejection of both modifier forms (with `_;` present so the return-argument error is the salient one). Lean witnesses pin the rejection AND the precision boundary: a bare `return;` in a modifier and a zero-return FUNCTION `return delete x;` (empty-but-non-null return list) both stay ACCEPTED.

cases.name: getter-nested-struct
cases.description: #63 (GET-STRUCT): solc's struct public-getter member-omission is SHALLOW. A nested struct member is returned WHOLE (including a dynamic array inside it), so `Outer public o` gets `o() returns (uint256 x, (uint256 a, uint256[] arr) inner)`. Forge asserts the getter tuple with real values; Lean imports the same contract, calls `set`, then the auto getter, and compares the returned (x, (a, arr)) source values.

evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.GetterNestedStruct.importedSourceUnit
  let target := "GetterNestedStructHarnessTarget"
  let w := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let setRes <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract 512 source target (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "set") SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [w 42, w 7, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.dynamicArray [w 100, w 200, w 300]]
  match setRes with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned s1 _ =>
      let getRes <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract 512 source target (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "o") s1 []
      let ok := match getRes with
        | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word x, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.tuple [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word a, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.dynamicArray [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word e0, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word e1, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word e2]]] =>
            SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq x 42 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq a 7 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq e0 100 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq e1 200 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq e2 300
        | _ => false

The control pins the boundary: top-level omission of a direct mapping+array keeps value/string members and returns a nested pure-value struct whole.

cases.name: mulmod-zero
cases.description: MULMOD0: a compile-time-CONSTANT zero modulus in addmod/mulmod (a literal 0, or a constant expression like 1-1 / 2*0 that solc's constant evaluator folds to zero) is Error 4195 "Arithmetic modulo zero" — a COMPILE error, not a runtime Panic. solidity-lean formerly ACCEPTED it and produced a runtime Panic 0x12. The fix mirrors the existing div/mod-by-zero constant-fold rejection: checkBuiltinIdentCall folds the modulus argument via numberLiteralRat? and rejects a constant that folds to zero, regardless of whether the other operands are constant. A NON-constant modulus (mulmod(2,3,m) with m a parameter) and a constant NON-zero modulus stay ACCEPTED; the runtime-zero case remains a runtime Panic 0x12. Pinned solc rejects the three invalid/ programs; forge deploys the accepted controls and asserts the runtime Panic 0x12 for a zero modulus and the folded values for non-zero; Lean imports the accepted controls and pins both sides of the tightened boundary via named witnesses.

cases.name: accept-boundary
cases.description: Two reject-fidelity fixes vs pinned solc 0.8.35. DIV-DUP-INH-MOD #81: base-constructor arguments given twice (once in the inheritance list, once in a constructor modifier), directly and across the linearization, are rejected. USINGFOR-BRACE #82: the brace-form using-for is validated eagerly — a non-attachable free function and a non-unique (overloaded) name are rejected. Pinned solc rejects all four invalid sources; the accept controls (single-supply base ctor, attachable+unique brace binding, unused library-form using-for which stays LAZY) plus every rejection are pinned in Lean via acceptBoundaryDisciplineMatches.

cases.name: reject-fidelity-2
cases.description: Two reject-fidelity fixes vs pinned solc 0.8.35. CMP-MIXEDSIGN #86: an opposite-sign folded integer-literal comparison ((0-1) < 1, ==, <=) has no common type and is rejected, while same-sign folded comparisons (1<2, (0-1)<(0-2)) still fold and accept. PRIV-SHADOW #69: a private function whose name+parameter types collide with a same-signature function in a strictly-inherited base (any visibility) is rejected ('Overriding function is missing override specifier'), while overloads (different params), different names, and legitimate public virtual/override still accept. Pinned solc rejects all five invalid sources; every rejection and accept control is pinned in Lean via rejectFidelity2Matches.

cases.name: dispatch-oom
cases.description: Forge, pinned solc, and imported Lean agree on the external-dispatch and try/catch success-return allocation-OOM boundary: an EAGER (memory) dynamic reference parameter (`bytes memory`, `uint256[] memory`) with a length above `0xffffffffffffffff` allocates before the calldata bounds check and raises Panic(0x41), while a LAZY (calldata) parameter with the same length keeps the empty `revert(0,0)`; a well-formed decode is unchanged. TC-OOM1: a successful try-call whose returndata carries an oversized dynamic length decodes in the success path to an UNCAUGHT Panic(0x41), whereas a genuinely-short returndata is an uncaught empty revert.

evals.label: importedExternalDispatchOomMatrix
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.DispatchOom.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "DispatchOom"
  let encodeWord := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeWord
  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let call := fun signature args => SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 256 contract SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty (selector signature ++ args)
  let panic41 := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector 0x4e487b71 ++ encodeWord 0x41
  let oversized := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord (2 ^ 64)
  let validBytes := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord 3 ++ [97, 98, 99] ++ List.replicate 29 0
  let memBytes <- call "memBytesLength(bytes)" oversized
  let calldataBytes <- call "calldataBytesLength(bytes)" oversized
  let memArray <- call "memUintArrayLength(uint256[])" oversized
  let calldataArray <- call "calldataUintArrayLength(uint256[])" oversized
  let validResult <- call "memBytesLength(bytes)" validBytes
  Except.ok (!memBytes.success && memBytes.output == panic41 && !calldataBytes.success && calldataBytes.output == [] && !memArray.success && memArray.output == panic41 && !calldataArray.success && calldataArray.output == [] && validResult.success && validResult.output == encodeWord 3))

evals.label: importedTryCatchSuccessReturnOomBoundary
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.DispatchOom.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "DispatchOom"
  let encodeWord := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeWord
  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let getBytesCalldata := selector "getBytes()"
  let hugeTarget := 0xd00d1
  let shortTarget := 0xd00d2
  let hugeOutput := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord (2 ^ 64)
  let shortOutput := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord 1
  let hugeCallResult : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult := { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.call, target := hugeTarget, calldata := getBytesCalldata, success := true, output := hugeOutput }
  let shortCallResult : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult := { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.call, target := shortTarget, calldata := getBytesCalldata, success := true, output := shortOutput }
  let context := { contract.core.context with accountCodes := [(hugeTarget, [0x60, 0x00]), (shortTarget, [0x60, 0x00])] }
  let hugeResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [hugeCallResult] []) contract "tryBytesLength" context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word hugeTarget]
  let shortResult <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [shortCallResult] []) contract "tryBytesLength" context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word shortTarget]
  let isPanic41 := fun result => match result with | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.panic c) => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq c 0x41 | _ => false
  let isEmpty := fun result => match result with | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.empty => true | _ => false
  Except.ok (isPanic41 hugeResult && isEmpty shortResult))

cases.name: dec-alloc-memptr
cases.description: DEC-ALLOC-MEMPTR (#114): the EAGER (memory) dynamic-reference decode allocation guard includes solc's running free-memory-pointer term. finalize_allocation (YulUtilFunctions.cpp:3256) panics 0x41 when `add(memPtr, roundUp(size)) > 0xffffffffffffffff` with memPtr (>= 0x80) the CURRENT free pointer, so a band of lengths BELOW the raw `elementSize*n + 0x20 > 2^64-1` bound still panics; arrayAllocationSizeFunction also rounds a BYTE length UP to a word. solc allocates BEFORE the calldata data-presence check (ABIFunctions.cpp:1184), so at memPtr=0x80 (external-dispatch decode) the panic is deterministic. Forge + pinned solc: an EAGER `uint256[] memory` at length 576460752303423486 and an EAGER `bytes memory` at length 2^64-33 (both inside the band, both below the old raw bound) revert Panic(0x41), while the LAZY calldata counterparts keep the empty revert(0,0) and a small decode is unchanged. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and drives the same matrix.

evals.label: importedDecAllocMemptrBandMatrix
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.DecAllocMemptr.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "DecAllocMemptr"
  let encodeWord := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeWord
  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let call := fun signature args => SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 256 contract SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty (selector signature ++ args)
  let panic41 := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector 0x4e487b71 ++ encodeWord 0x41
  let arrayBand := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord 576460752303423486
  let bytesBand := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord 18446744073709551583
  let validArray := encodeWord 0x20 ++ encodeWord 3 ++ encodeWord 10 ++ encodeWord 20 ++ encodeWord 30
  let memArray <- call "memUintArrayLength(uint256[])" arrayBand
  let calldataArray <- call "calldataUintArrayLength(uint256[])" arrayBand
  let memBytes <- call "memBytesLength(bytes)" bytesBand
  let calldataBytes <- call "calldataBytesLength(bytes)" bytesBand
  let validResult <- call "memUintArrayLength(uint256[])" validArray
  Except.ok (!memArray.success && memArray.output == panic41 && !calldataArray.success && calldataArray.output == [] && !memBytes.success && memBytes.output == panic41 && !calldataBytes.success && calldataBytes.output == [] && validResult.success && validResult.output == encodeWord 3))

cases.name: store-tail-clear
cases.description: STORE-TAIL-CLEAR (G): a whole-aggregate storage assignment whose TOP layout is a struct or fixedArray must recurse and ZERO the shrunk tail element slots of every dynamic-array member (solc copy_struct_to_storage -> copy_array_to_storage -> resize_array -> cleanup_storage_array_end -> clear_storage_range). solidity-lean formerly tail-zeroed only a top-level dynamic array; a struct/fixedArray top fell through to a plain store that left the shrunk tail STALE. Routing struct AND fixedArray tops through the existing deep-store recursion (storeStorageLayoutAtWithDeepClear) fixes it. The Lean evals read the raw tail slots off the post-call state (the stale tail is invisible to length-bounded getters); the Forge side pins the solc/EVM getter values.

evals.label: structShrinkTailZeroed
storageToStorageShrinkTailZeroed

(do
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.ownCall 512 SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.StoreTailClear.importedContract (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "storageToStorageShrink") SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []

  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned st [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word len, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word e0, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word e1] =>
      let t2 := st.loadSlot (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.dynamicArrayStorageSlot 1 2)
      let t4 := st.loadSlot (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.dynamicArrayStorageSlot 1 4)
      Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq len 2 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq e0 111 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq e1 222 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq t2 0 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq t4 0)
  | _ => Except.ok false)

cases.name: narrow-bitwise-cleanup
cases.description: NARROW-BITWISE (F1/F2): a bitwise op (`<<`, `~`) on a narrow (<256-bit) uintN/intN cleans at its OPERAND width with a truncating cast (solc `cleanup_t_uintN`=`and`, `cleanup_t_intN`=`signextend`), never a checked range-check, and that operand-width clean survives widening. F1: `x<<k` widened cleans at the LHS width first (a(255)=240, b(64)=-128). F2: `~x` on a narrow unsigned masks and never Panics 0x11 (c(0)=255, d(0)=255). Controls pin no regression: same-width `<<` unchanged (shlSameWidth 255=240), checked ARITHMETIC overflow STILL Panics 0x11 (addOverflow 200), `~uint256(0)` full-width no-op mask = 2^256-1, `~intN` unchanged (notInt 5=-6).
