cases.name: lib-storage-public
cases.description: A public library function taking a `T storage` pointer, invoked both via using-for (`arr.pushPub(v)`) and directly (`L.pushPub(arr, v)`), plus a `view` read-back (`arr.sumPub()`). solc 0.8.35 lowers these to DELEGATECALLs whose calldata carries the storage SLOT of the pointer (not the array contents) and whose selector includes ` storage` in the signature (`pushPub(uint256[] storage,uint256)` = 0x8ba1851b, `sumPub(uint256[] storage)` = 0x15833f22). Forge pins the real-EVM storage effect and read-backs; imported Lean pins the delegatecall calldata (selector + slot) the model emits on the external-library boundary.

evals.label: importedLibStoragePublicStoragePointerDelegatecall
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.LibStoragePublic.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "LibStoragePublic"
  let word := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let ctx := { contract.core.context with contractAddresses := [("L", 0xbeef)], accountCodes := [(0xbeef, [1])] }
  let pushCalldata := fun (v : Nat) => do
    let enc <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues
      [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256]
      [word 0, word v]
    Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature "pushPub(uint256[] storage,uint256)") ++ enc)
  let sumEnc <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word 0]
  let sumCalldata := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature "sumPub(uint256[] storage)") ++ sumEnc
  let sumOut <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word 12]
  let runPush := fun (fn : String) (v : Nat) => do
    let cd <- pushCalldata v
    let oracle : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
      { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall
        target := 0xbeef, calldata := cd, value := 0, gas? := none
        success := true, output := [] }
    let r <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [oracle] []) contract fn ctx
      SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [word v]
    match r with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state _ =>
        match state.externalInteractions with
        | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
            Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall 0xbeef cd 0 none && call.success)
        | _ => Except.ok false
    | _ => Except.ok false
  let usingOk <- runPush "viaUsing" 5
  let directOk <- runPush "viaDirect" 7
  let sumOracle : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
    { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall
      target := 0xbeef, calldata := sumCalldata, value := 0, gas? := none
      success := true, output := sumOut }
  let tr <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256
    (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [sumOracle] []) contract "total" ctx
    SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  let totalOk := match tr with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word v] =>
        match state.externalInteractions with
        | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
            SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v 12 &&
            SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall 0xbeef sumCalldata 0 none
        | _ => false
    | _ => false
  Except.ok (usingOk && directOk && totalOk))

cases.name: named-arg-order
cases.description: NAMED-ARG-ORDER regression pin. solc 0.8.35 LEGACY codegen (corpus ground truth) evaluates a call's NAMED arguments in the callee's PARAMETER/DECLARATION order, then binds by name; solc via-IR instead evaluates them in SOURCE (call-site) order (verified on real EVM: an internal call `twoI({b: e1, a: e2})` runs `e2` (param a, declared first) before `e1` (param b) under legacy => order digits 21, whereas via-IR gives 12). solidity-lean lowers an internal call's named arguments into per-parameter temporaries evaluated in parameter order (the boundaryArgDecls / toExprsForParams? path), so it ALREADY matches LEGACY -- no model change was needed. This lane guarantees the model keeps legacy parameter-order semantics for internal named arguments and does not drift to the via-IR source order. Each argument is an assignment expression `trace = trace*10+n` (order-observable, not a nested call). Scenarios: positionalOrder pins the shared source-order path (12); internalOrder pins 2-arg named parameter order (21); internalThree pins 3-arg named parameter order with a scrambled {c,a,b} call site (231, unambiguously parameter order vs the source order 123). Values captured on real EVM via Forge and re-checked by the Forge test; Lean imports the same source and runs the source semantics via own-call. Named-argument syntax is only accepted by solc for function calls / struct constructors / events / errors (NOT modifier or base-constructor invocations, which are rejected at parse); struct/event/error named args route through the ABI/component encoder whose child evaluation order is a separate independently-tracked concern, so this lane covers only the encoder-decoupled internal-call path.

cases.name: lib-storage-public-2
cases.description: A public library function `pushPub(uint256[] storage,uint256)` taking a `T storage` pointer, invoked with storage-pointer ARGUMENTS that are not bare top-level state variables: a MAPPING VALUE `m[k]` (direct `L2.pushPub(m[k], v)`), a STRUCT-MEMBER array `s.a` (using-for `s.a.pushPub(v)`), and a `T storage` LOCAL bound to a nested-array element (`uint256[] storage p = aa[i]; L2.pushPub(p, v)`). solc 0.8.35 encodes each `T storage self` as the pointer's runtime-computed storage SLOT in the delegatecall calldata (keccak256(k.slot_m) for the mapping value, the additive field slot for the struct member, keccak256(slot_aa)+i for the nested-array element). Before LIB-STORAGE-PUBLIC-2 the model over-rejected these at the executable-lowering boundary (`coreStoragePointerSlotExpr?` returned `none` for any non-`Expr.storage` storage lvalue). Forge pins the real-EVM storage effect (read-backs of m[k], s.a, aa[i] after the library push); imported Lean pins that the contract now lowers AND emits a delegatecall whose calldata carries exactly the resolved slot (selector `pushPub(uint256[] storage,uint256)` + slot word + value word) for all three shapes.

evals.label: importedLibStoragePublic2StoragePointerDelegatecall
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.LibStoragePublic2.importedSourceUnit
  let program <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract
    (<- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source) "LibStoragePublic2"
  let word := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let ctx := { program.core.context with contractAddresses := [("L2", 0xbeef)], accountCodes := [(0xbeef, [1])] }
  let mkCd := fun (slot v : Nat) => do
    let enc <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues
      [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.uint256] [word slot, word v]
    Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature "pushPub(uint256[] storage,uint256)") ++ enc)
  let runOne := fun (fn : String) (cd : List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Byte) (st : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State) (args : List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value) => do
    let oracle : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
      { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall
        target := 0xbeef, calldata := cd, value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := [] }
    let r <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256
      (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [oracle] []) program fn ctx st args
    match r with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state _ =>
        match state.externalInteractions with
        | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
            Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call
              SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall 0xbeef cd 0 none && call.success)
        | _ => Except.ok false
    | _ => Except.ok false
  let structCd <- mkCd 1 99
  let structOk <- runOne "pushStruct" structCd SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [word 99]
  let mapCd <- mkCd (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.mappingStorageSlot 0 3) 22
  let mapOk <- runOne "pushMapping" mapCd SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [word 3, word 22]
  let localCd <- mkCd (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.dynamicArrayStorageSlot 2 0) 77
  let dummy : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult :=
    { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.delegatecall
      target := 0xbeef, calldata := localCd, value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := [] }
  let ra <- SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 256
    (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [dummy] []) program "addRow" ctx SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  let stateA := match ra with
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned state _ => state
    | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted state _ => state
  let localOk <- runOne "pushLocal" localCd stateA [word 0, word 77]
  Except.ok (structOk && mapOk && localOk))

cases.name: callpos-family
cases.description: CALLPOS-FAMILY closes the remaining still-reachable call-position over-rejects after the boundary-completion arc: MULTIPLE direct-call arguments in one call (f(g(), h()), f(g(), 10, h())) and NESTED call arguments (f(g(h())), f(f(g())), f(g(h()), 1)). The earlier single-argument hoist peeled only the FIRST direct-call argument, so these two shapes stayed over-rejecting (solc 0.8.35 legacy accepts+compiles each; the model returned none at Source->Executable). Fix: FunctionDecl.hoistDirectInternalCallArgs? hoists EVERY direct-call argument (nested-first, then left-to-right) into ordered prefix temps, wired into the call-statement / return / single- and multi-binding varDecl arms; the pre-existing specialized f(first, g()) call-statement arm (which only hoisted the second arg) was removed as the general hoist subsumes it. solc evaluates call arguments left-to-right and a nested call before its enclosing call (verified via --ir); the prefix reproduces that. Everything is own-call executable (internal calls + a state var), so acceptance AND runtime are pinned by own-contract execution, including two eval-order pins (multiArgOrder=12 needs gA() before hB(); nestOrder=133 needs innermost-first). A call-free control pins the pre-existing pure path; the Forge test re-checks every case against real solc/EVM.

cases.name: calldata-lazy-value
cases.description: Forge/real-EVM ground truth that solc defers ALL value-element validation of a CALLDATA-location array/struct to ACCESS time: abiDecodingFunctionCalldataArray/...Struct read no value elements at the dispatch boundary (only length + stride bound checks) and return a calldata pointer, so a DIRTY value element (a bool word == 2, an address with dirty high bits, a dirty static struct member) that the body never reads does NOT revert; the same element reverts empty (validator_revert_*) the moment it is accessed. Forge drives hand-built calldata carrying the dirty element for both the not-accessed (success) and accessed (empty revert) cases across bool[], address[], and a fully-static calldata struct. Lean imports the same contract and checks the interpreter's calldata dispatch defers value-element validation to access (substituting a calldataDeferredInvalid marker) instead of over-rejecting at the boundary.

(do

cases.name: common-type-literal
cases.description: Forge checks the real-EVM value of a binary op whose operands are a narrow typed integer and an untyped number LITERAL that does NOT fit it (#109 COMMON-TYPE-LITERAL-MOBILE). solc computes the common type as commonType(narrow, literal->mobileType()) using the literal's SMALLEST-fitting uintN/intN (300 -> uint16, 70000 -> uint24), NOT uint256, so checked arithmetic runs at that narrow width: uint8 a*300 Panics 0x11 for a>=219 (a=255 -> 76500 > 65535) yet returns the fitting value otherwise; uint8 a+300 really is uint16 (so it returns as uint16 -- the over-reject twin solc accepts); uint16 a*70000 runs at uint24. solidity-lean formerly widened the literal to uint256, ran the op at 256 bits, missed the overflow Panic and mis-typed the result. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST.

cases.name: neg-literal-common-type
cases.description: NEGATIVE-literal sibling of #109 (#111 NEG-LITERAL-COMMON-TYPE). A negative untyped number literal's mobileType is the smallest-fitting SIGNED intN (-300 -> int16, -1 -> int8), and solc forbids all signed<->unsigned implicit conversions (Types.cpp:611-614), so `uint8 a * -300` has NO common type and solc REJECTS it (a rejection witness, not a runtime lane). A SIGNED operand shares the common type: `int16 a * -300` runs the checked op at int16, overflowing to Panic 0x11 (a=200 -> -60000, a=-200 -> 60000) yet returning the fitting signed value otherwise; `int8 a * -1` is the INT8_MIN negation overflow (a=-128 -> 128 Panics). This lane exercises the accepted signed-operand side that solc emits an AST for; solidity-lean already handles both sides (A1 signed/unsigned rule composed with the #109 mobile-type widening). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST.

  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.AbiEncodeLitFixedBytes.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "AbiLitFactory"
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [] [ { contractName := "AbiLitDynC", constructorArgs := args, value := 0, salt? := none, success := true, address := 0xcafe } ]) contract "makeDyn" contract.core.context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word address] =>
      match (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.resultState result).externalInteractions with
      | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.contractCreation create] =>
          Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq address 0xcafe && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ContractCreationResult.matches create "AbiLitDynC" args 0 none && create.success)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  | _ => Except.ok false)

evals.expr:
(do
  let encoded ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedAbiEncodeValues [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Ty.fixedBytes 2] [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 0xabcd]
  let calldata := ([0xa7, 0xab, 0xdc, 0x09] : List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Byte) ++ encoded
  let row : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult := { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall, target := 0xc0ffee, calldata := calldata, value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := encoded }
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.AbiEncodeLitFixedBytes.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "AbiLitFactory"
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.responderOfResults [row] []) contract "callF" contract.core.context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word 0xc0ffee]
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word ret] =>
      match (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.resultState result).externalInteractions with
      | [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ExternalInteraction.lowLevelCall call] =>
          Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq ret 0xabcd && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult.matches call SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall 0xc0ffee calldata 0 none && call.success)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  | _ => Except.ok false)
